Conditional independence makes distinct-particle C(t)=Cov(V0,Vt), valid for N>=2 and fixed-lag N→∞ empirical limits. Reconstructed phase-resolved stationary m=-2D(Q-2diag)^{-1}pi and z=-4D(Q-4diag)^{-1}m and verified C0=D²(a-b)²P/(K²J), W=E[Vdot²]=4D²r(a-b)²(a+b+r)/(KJ); C′(0)=0, C′′(0+)=-W. The 4-component two-time system u′=Qu, w′=(Q-2diag)w+2Du yields characteristic exponents 2r and a+b+r ± sqrt(r²+(a-b)²); exact residues follow from the 3 initial conditions. Algebra confirms A_s=D²(a-b)²/[K(2ab-r(a+b))] and the ordering/strict positive slowest residues either side of r*=2ab/(a+b). At equality the direct Laplace transform has a NONZERO genuine second-order pole and T=D²(a-b)²/[K(a+b-r*)]>0, yielding t e^{-2r*t}. Independently recomputed symbolic C0, W, environment residue, collision T and exact rational a=2,b=2/3,r=1,D=1 sample (79/600+t/5)e^{-2t}-19/1600 e^{-16t/3}. A separately formed block-matrix exponential matched the scalar law in 900 independent random positive-parameter/lag comparisons; max absolute error 3.64e-12. Finite tests only corroborate analytic identities. Boundaries: equal a=b gives zero collective covariance; r>0, a,b,D>0 and stationary initialization are essential; no asymmetric switching or interacting particles.
